name: Seance
lede: Seance is a deep violet whose name is a word for a sitting, usually a spirit-medium's.

sections.title: A name with no recorded story
sections.body: None of the 29 books in our reference set uses it as a color name; the hits are the French word *séances* inside journal citations [1]. Who first applied the word to this violet is undocumented in our sources. Rather than guess at a story, we leave it blank [1]. The word itself is French for a sitting, and its use for a spirit-medium's meeting is a separate matter from the color [1]. Any link between the two would be our inference, not a recorded fact [1].

sections.title: The swatch
sections.body: The swatch is #612086, a dark, saturated violet [2]. It sits near [[purple]] and [[violet]], darker and bluer than [[wisteria]] and [[mauve]].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our name graph records Seance with ISCC-NBS 1955 as the earliest source date, plus a wiki list entry [2]. No painting in our archive of 23,781 has this color covering at least 1 per cent of its canvas, within a CIEDE2000 distance of 4, as photographed [3]. That describes this archive, not painting as a whole [3].

notes.cite: Concordance check of 29 color books: only "séances" in citations (Pastoureau, Green, ch. 48; Pigment Compendium, p. 492)

questions.q: Do our reference books say who named this color?
True or false: Seance is darker than Wisteria.

openers: Not every color name has a story, and this one has none on record.
